questions.q: Who does David ask listen to what he says and understand his murmuring?
questions.a: David asks Yahweh to listen to what he says and understand his distressed sigh.

questions.q: What names does David use for the one who listens to the sound of his cry?
questions.a: David calls him his king and his God.

questions.q: What does David say he will do each morning?
questions.a: David says he will prepare for Yahweh and watch.

questions.q: What does God certainly not do?
questions.a: He certainly does not approve of evil, and evil people will not be his guests.

questions.q: Who will not stand in God’s presence?
questions.a: The arrogant will not stand in God’s presence.
God hates all who do evil things.

questions.q: What will God do to liars?

questions.a: Yahweh despises violent and deceitful men.

questions.q: Why will David come into Yahweh’s house?
questions.a: David will come into Yahweh’s house because of Yahweh’s great covenant faithfulness.

questions.q: How will David bow down toward Yahweh’s holy temple?
questions.a: David will bow down in reverence.

questions.q: Why does David ask Yahweh to guide him in righteousness?
questions.a: David asks Yahweh to guide him in righteousness because of those who are watching him.

questions.q: How does David describe his enemies?
questions.a: David describes his enemies as untrustworthy, desiring to destroy people, speaking things that are vile like the smell of an open grave, and flattering people to trap and destroy them.

questions.q: What does David ask God to do to his enemies because of their many transgressions and their rebellion against God?
questions.a: David asks God to declare his enemies guilty and to drive them out.

questions.q: Why should those who take refuge in God shout for joy?
questions.a: They should shout for joy because God defends them.

questions.q: What will Yahweh do for the righteous?
questions.a: Yahweh will bless the righteous and surround them with his favor as with a shield.

commentary.text: God will certainly hear prayer: David gives to God the glory, and takes to himself the comfort.
He prayed for himself, that God would guide him, and for all the Lord's people, that God would give them joy, and keep them safe.

Verses 1–6 God is a prayer-hearing God. Such he has always been, and he is still as ready to hear prayer as ever. The most encouraging principle of prayer, and the most powerful plea in prayer, is, to look upon him as our King and our God. David also prays to a sin-hating God. sin is folly, and sinners are the greatest of all fools; fools of their own making. Wicked people hate God; justly are they hated of him, and this will be their endless misery and ruin. Let us learn the importance of truth and sincerity, in all the affairs of life. Liars and murderers resemble the devil, and are his children, therefore it may well be expected that God should abhor them. These were the characters of David's enemies; and such as these are still the enemies of Christ and his people.

David prayed often alone, yet was very constant in attendance on public worship. The mercy of God should ever be the foundation both of our hope and of our joy, in every thing wherein we have to do with him. Let us learn to pray, not for ourselves only, but for others; grace be with all that love Christ in sincerity. The Divine blessing comes down upon us through Jesus Christ, the righteous or just One, as of old it did upon Israel through David, whom God protected, and placed upon the throne. Thou, O Christ, art the righteous Saviour, thou art the King of Israel, thou art the Fountain of blessing to all believers; thy favour is the defence and protection of thy church.
